acceptance.statement: `extensions/index.ts` no longer defines `resolveTool` (or its comment block); `registerNamedTool` is the only lazy tool-registration wrapper, and every registered tool keeps its runtime-derived prompt metadata (existing tool-registration tests and `scripts/smoke-pi-package.mjs` stay green).

Denied and successful operations emit records built by the same private builder: `authorize()` contains no inline `AuditRecord` literal, and the denial record still carries operation, initiator, workspace, `policyAuthorized: false`, `policyDenialReason`, `outputTruncated` and `commandCapture`.

`buildChildEnvironment` rejects a disallowed environment name with a `RuntimeError` of kind `policy-denied` (never a bare `Error`), so `errorKindOf` returns `policy-denied` while the message still names the offending variable.
The transient selection state reports a non-stopped error kind of its own with the retry remedy instead of `target-stopped`, and the status-to-kind mapping is exercised by a unit test in `bind()`.

`redactText` replaces whole authentication values (`Bearer|Basic|Token` plus everything up to whitespace) and whole bare secret values; regression cases containing `,`, `;`, `:` quotes and CJK characters assert that no tail of the credential survives, and the existing redaction cases still pass.

One shared spawn-error mapper and one shared bounded-invocation helper serve `docker-adapter`, `docker-lifecycle` and `devcontainer-adapter`; the six compile-time-only `unreachable … path` throws are gone; per-tool kind mapping is preserved (docker executable missing yields `daemon-unavailable`, devcontainer executable missing yields `devcontainer-cli-failure`, permission denied yields `authorization-denied`).
A failed `docker stop`/`docker rm` reports a Docker-specific failure kind (never `devcontainer-cli-failure`) and carries the exit code, asserted by adapter unit tests.

The runtime layer exports the single named default output cap and the adapters import it instead of declaring their own literals; the 256 KiB logs cap becomes a named constant; production behaviour is unchanged because every production call site still passes `config.maxOutputBytes`.

No behaviour regression: `npm run typecheck`, the full unit suite and `node scripts/verify-package.mjs --unit-tests` pass, and the committed `dist` is rebuilt so CI's committed-output freshness check stays green.
